title: Reflection of Light
subject: Physics
objective: The Moon makes no light, yet it shines at night: sunlight bounces off it to our eyes. That bouncing back is reflection.

fill.q: Light returning into the same medium after striking a surface is ____.
Objects that make their own light are ____.
In a dark room even a white wall cannot be seen because there is no ____.

tf.q: The Sun is a non-luminous object.
We see a book by the light it reflects.
Reflection can happen without any light falling on a surface.

ar.a: A white wall is invisible in a dark room.
ar.r: There is no light for the wall to reflect.

ar.explain: A is false; R is true.

mcq.q: We see a non-luminous object because it:
In a dark room a white wall is invisible because:
options: no light falls on it to reflect

short.q: Distinguish luminous and non-luminous objects with two examples each.
short.solution: Luminous make light: Sun, bulb. Non-luminous are seen by reflected light: Moon, book.

short.q: Why is the Moon visible at night?
short.solution: It reflects sunlight towards the Earth.

left: Light bouncing back into the same medium
match.explain: Most things we see are seen by reflected light.
